name: rekora-relevance-v1
notes: Synthetic project memory for a fictional order-management system. Labels were written by hand: each answerable question names the single memory key that answers it. Questions deliberately mix exact wording, paraphrase, Spanish and identifier lookups, so keyword-only retrieval is expected to miss some.

memories.content: Order updates use optimistic concurrency with a rowversion column; conflicting writes return HTTP 409.
Order updates take a pessimistic row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) for the whole request.
The orders API must answer in under 200 ms at p95 for lists of up to 100 orders.
Authentication uses short-lived JWT access tokens (15 minutes) plus rotating refresh tokens stored server-side.
CSV export of orders times out above 10k rows because it loads everything in memory; needs streaming.
Fixed the flaky OrderServiceTests by freezing the clock with a FakeTimeProvider instead of DateTime.UtcNow.
Team prefers small pull requests under 400 changed lines, reviewed within one working day.
Front end is Vue 3 with Pinia for state and Vite for builds.
The database is SQL Server 2022; migrations are managed with EF Core.
Never log personal data: emails, phone numbers and addresses must be masked in logs.
Prices are stored as decimal(18,4) in the tenant currency; never use floating point for money.
Release procedure: tag vX.Y.Z on main, CI builds the container, then promote to staging and run smoke tests before production.
Safari 16 drops the auth cookie on cross-site redirects; the login page must be same-site.
Background jobs run on Hangfire with SQL Server storage; retries are capped at 5 attempts.
Multi-tenancy is implemented with a TenantId column on every table and a global EF query filter.
Public API changes require a version bump; v1 endpoints stay supported for 12 months after v2 ships.
Search over products uses Azure AI Search; the SQL LIKE fallback was removed.
Daylight saving change duplicates the 01:00-02:00 hour in the delivery slot report.
Store all timestamps in UTC and convert to the tenant time zone only in the UI to fix the delivery slot duplicates.
Payment provider is Stripe; webhooks are verified with the signing secret from Key Vault.
Feature flags are managed with a simple FeatureFlags table, not a third-party service.
Container images must be built from the distroless base and scanned with Trivy before deploy.
Invoices are generated as PDF with QuestPDF and archived in blob storage for 10 years.
The OrderEditor component re-renders on every keystroke because the whole order object is reactive.
Use shallowRef for the order in OrderEditor and debounce saves to 500 ms to stop excessive re-renders.
Inventory reservations expire after 30 minutes if checkout is not completed.
Email notifications are sent through SendGrid templates owned by the marketing team.
Commit messages are written in Spanish with a short summary line and a detailed body.
Unit tests must not hit the network; integration tests use Testcontainers for SQL Server.
Shipping cost is calculated by the carrier rate service; we cache quotes for 10 minutes.
The warehouse scanner app is a .NET MAUI client that syncs every 5 minutes.
Discount codes may apply twice when the cart is updated in two tabs at once.
Discount codes are validated and consumed inside the order transaction to prevent double use.
Observability uses OpenTelemetry traces exported to Grafana Tempo; logs go to Loki.
Customer data must stay in the EU region (West Europe) for GDPR compliance.
To rotate the Stripe webhook secret: create the new secret, deploy with both secrets accepted, then revoke the old one.
Returns are handled as a separate ReturnOrder aggregate linked to the original order id.
Product images are resized on upload to 1600px and served from a CDN as WebP.
Stream the CSV export with IAsyncEnumerable and write rows directly to the response to fix the export timeout.
Rate limiting on the public API is 100 requests per minute per API key using the built-in ASP.NET Core limiter.
